headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Replit Agent can write broad Repl files while PaddleOCR can ingest document content, creating leakage and conflict risks; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection path is not documented, but B can write Repl workspace files and A can process documents/images from files or APIs. If B places attacker-controlled text into files that A later ingests, prompt-like content could influence A. This is lower than medium because no shared clipboard/MCP is shown and A is not a general agent.
conditions: IF B writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file that A later reads as document input
IF A is configured to ingest workspace files produced by B
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Add a file allowlist for A inputs
Strip instruction-like text before A ingestion
Use a human review step before passing B outputs to A

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad filesystem/network access; A touches documents and images and can egress to allowlisted network destinations. A shared Repl workspace is plausible because B's filesystem persists across sessions, so sensitive material could flow from B into A's processing path. This is medium because the leakage path exists in default-style workspace use, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace files
IF B stores secrets or deployment config in files that A can read or process
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Move A to a separate project or container
Redact sensitive files before A runs
Restrict A input paths to non-sensitive directories
Rotate any secrets exposed in workspace files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write files, execute shell, and modify git state; A can call APIs and run browsers, but its write surface is not shown. The main conflict is on shared mutable workspace state if both touch the same Repl files or repo. Because A's write capability is not explicit, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A and B modify the same repository or workspace files
IF B commits or rewrites git state while A is reading or generating artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate branches to A and B
Pause B before A writes outputs
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Disable git writes for one agent during joint runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on workspace content and modify git state, so if it consumes A's OCR output as authoritative, transcription errors can cascade into code or deployment changes. A is a document-processing agent, not a verifier, and B's tool access makes downstream mistakes consequential. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A's extracted text as authoritative input
IF B applies A's output to code, deployment, or git changes without review
mitigations: Require manual verification of A outputs before B acts
Compare OCR output against source documents
Limit B to draft-only changes
Add checksum or citation checks for extracted text

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration, while A processes documents and images and can egress to allowlisted network destinations. If regulated or sensitive documents are OCR'd by A and then stored or transformed in B's Repl workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF B retains workspace artifacts longer than the source system's policy
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of the shared Repl workspace
Set short retention for generated artifacts
Document a deletion/export procedure for workspace files
